newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu slams Palestinian plans to declare state.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu slams Palestinian plans to declare state.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday slammed President Yasser Arafat's intention to declare a Palestinian state in two years' time.

"The prime minister said the unilateral declaration of the Palestinian Authority on the establishment of a state is a breach of the agreement and a grave error on its part and we are prepared for this possibility," a statement issued after the weekly cabinet meeting said.

PLO head Arafat, elected president of the Palestinian Authority running the self-rule enclaves in the West Bank and Gaza Strip set up under Israel-Palestinian interim peace accords, made the comment in a radio interview.
Asked by Europe-1 when a Palestinian state would exist, Arafat replied: "As soon as the interim period is over, we shall declare our Palestinian state. In two years' time."

Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) signed a framework for peace in September 1993. In May 1994, they signed an accord that set up the first self-rule enclaves and said talks on a final peace settlement were to begin within two years and last up to three years.

The talks began under Israel's previous government in May. Netanyahu ousted the centre-left government in elections on May 29 and final status peace talks have not resumed. Netanyahu opposes establishment of a Palestinian state.
